Immediate data.

A `naga::Module` may contain at most one `naga::GlobalVariable` in
this address space. Its contents are provided not by a buffer
but by `SetImmediates` pass commands, allowing the CPU to
establish different values for each draw/dispatch.

`Immediate` variables may not contain `f16` values, even if
the `SHADER_FLOAT16` capability is enabled.

Backends generally place tight limits on the size of
`Immediate` variables.

EntryPoint.description: Reflection information for one entry point.

immediateUsage.description: The immediate data this entry point uses.

outputs.description:
Stage outputs, with structs flattened. For mesh shaders, this also holds the
per-vertex and per-primitive outputs.

rayTracingPayload.description: The type of the ray tracing payload, for ray tracing stages.

resources.description: The resources this entry point statically uses.

samplingPairs.description: (texture, sampler) pairs this entry point samples with.

taskPayloadSize.description: Size of the task payload, for task and mesh shaders that use one.

workgroupSize.description: The workgroup size, for compute-like stages. `[0, 0, 0]` for other stages.

workgroupSizeFromOverrides.description:
For each dimension, whether the workgroup size is given by an override
expression. Such dimensions hold a placeholder in [`Self::workgroup_size`] until
overrides are applied.

workgroupStorageSize.description: Bytes of `workgroup` memory used, with each variable rounded up to 16 bytes.

ImmediateSlots.description:
A bitmask, tracking which 4-byte slots have been written via `set_immediates`.
Bit N corresponds to bytes [N*4 .. N*4+4).
